who: two townsfolk at a stall, a buyer and a seller

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two pennies for that loaf? It was a halfpenny at harvest.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then go back to harvest. The granary's near bare.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {steward} sits on full sacks, I'd wager.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wager with what? You can't afford bread.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Weigh it again. Your thumb's on the scale.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My thumb's the only fat thing in {town} this month.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fair price on the {good} today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fair? Remember you said that when it climbs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three of everything, and a ribbon for my girl.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Look at you, spending like a lord's cousin.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Granary's full, roads are clear. Let a woman enjoy it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {good}'s up by half since the news.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Shortage, they say. Shortage of honest sellers, more like.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Carts lost on the road again. Prices jump by evening.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then buy now, before the hoarders wake up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sunward prices. Even the flies pay a toll here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the water costs more than the wine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Clan iron, clan bread, clan prices. Outsiders pay double.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then keep your mouth shut. Your accent costs a penny a word.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How much?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Depends who's asking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Me. Same as every week, {B}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then the same price. Don't haggle, it bores me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: End of the day. Give me the bruised ones cheap.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bruised costs the same. Rotten costs less. Come back tomorrow.

who: two stallholders side by side

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Help me with the awning, it's sagging.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Everything in {town} sags. Pull the left rope.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nobody's buying. They're only looking.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Looking's free. It's all anyone can afford.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Third day running the stall's empty by noon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Raise your prices. They'll still pay.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Greedy.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Thriving, I call it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hamlet folk aren't coming in. The raid scared them off.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fewer sellers, better prices for us. Grim, but true.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Damp's in the cloth again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Damp's in everything here. Even the coin feels wet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Watch the stall, I need a piss.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: If something walks off, it's your loss.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then keep your eyes open, {B}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pack it up before the cutpurses come out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The cutpurses are the watch. They just work days.

who: two travellers stocking up before a journey

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hard bread, dried meat and a skin of water.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Going far?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Far enough that I won't be back for more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half rations for the road, then.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Half of half. {steward} won't sell more to travellers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Buy extra. If the road shuts, we wait it out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wait where? Under a cart, with the outlaws for company?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Water first. Food second. Everything else after.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Water first in the desert. So you've learned something.

who: two household servants doing the day's marketing

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The lady's list is longer than my arm.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Her list, her coin. Your feet, though.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cook says come back with meat or don't come back.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we're not going back. There's no meat.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Saffron, figs and a capon. Who's she feeding?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Someone she wants to impress. Ask no questions.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Turnips again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Turnips are honest. Nobody ever stabbed a man over a turnip.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Steward wants salt. There's none to be had.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then he gets a story about salt instead.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you get the eggs?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Two broke on the way.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So we tell Cook the hen was lazy.

who: two merchants striking a bargain

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {good} for your cloth. Straight swap.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Straight? Mine's dyed. Yours is dusty.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dust washes off, dye fades. We're even.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'll trade you anything for grain.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Anything is what everyone offers. Grain is what nobody has.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Grain's dear, so wool's cheap. Bad week to be a shepherd.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every week's a bad week to be a shepherd.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Granary's full. Grain's worth nothing here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then cart it somewhere hungry. Somewhere always is.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The smiths posted a buy order for ore.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Above base price? Then I buy ore today and sell tomorrow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Carts lost. {good} will be dear within a fortnight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we hold ours and smile at the buyers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sir John the Coin taxes every bale twice.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Once for the road, once for breathing near him.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ingots for salt fish. Clan rate.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'm not clan.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the rate is: you pay more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Order's filled. {good} will drop now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sell before the carriers get back and tell everyone.

who: a baker and a helper at the bread stall

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bread's half bran and half sawdust.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And all of it gone by dawn. Nobody cares.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Honey loaves today. Sold out by noon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bake twice, then. While flour's cheap.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Warm bread! Fresh from the oven!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yesterday's, sprinkled with water.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep your voice down.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ovens hot since the middle of the night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And still the first in line complain.

who: an alewife and her daughter

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good brown ale, a penny a jug.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Watered?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rained in. That's a different thing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No barley, so no ale. It's well water and prayer.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sell the prayer. It's cheaper to make.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Brother says ale's a sin before Vespers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Brother drinks after Vespers. I keep his tab.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fill the guild lads' cups. They pay in silver.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Silver tonight. Promises tomorrow.

who: a butcher and a customer

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fresh mutton, killed this morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Which morning?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A morning. Do you want it or not?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's not mutton.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's meat. In a starving town, don't ask what kind.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wolves took a hamlet's flock. Mutton's dear now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Dear for us. Cheap for the wolves.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Venison from the lord's hunt. The leavings.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A lord's leavings feed a whole street.

who: a pie-seller and a hungry neighbour

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hot pies! Pork and onion!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mostly onion.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Onion's real. Pork's a rumour.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Smaller pies, same price.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They'll notice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They'll notice hunger more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sell the last ones to the drunks.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Drunks can't count. Charge them double.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eel pies sold out again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Full bellies make for more bellies. Bake more tomorrow.

who: a shopkeeper and an apprentice counting stock

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Count the sacks again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Twelve. Same as before.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Count again. Twelve is what the thief wants me to think.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We're three bolts of {good} short.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Rats?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rats with two legs and a key.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stores are full to the rafters.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then stop buying. We can't sell it fast enough.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hide half the {good} in the cellar.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hoarding?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Waiting. Prices are about to climb.

who: a shopkeeper and a customer

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What'll it be?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Same as always.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Same as always costs more now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Since when? Since you saw me coming?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No credit. Not this week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I've bought here ten years!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And I've starved here one. No credit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pay half now, half after harvest.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: After harvest you'll forget me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I never forget a debt, {B}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Coin's flowing, friend. Something for your wife?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Something for me first. She can wait.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That one's a friend of {player}. Give them the fair price.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's a fair price? Since when?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {player} was in here earlier.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Did you serve them?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I served them the door.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: First Hearth bread, first quality. Fit for a king.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's no king.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then fit for whoever's next.

who: a farmer and his wife at their cart

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cabbages, leeks, the last of the beans.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bring the beans forward. Beans sell.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Townsfolk followed the cart from the gate.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sell fast, and get home before they follow us there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Too many turnips. Can't give them away.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Feed them to the pigs, then sell the pigs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hamlet's burned. This is all we saved.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then ask double. The town needs it more than we do.

who: two traders buying stock

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Buy the {good} cheap here, sell it dear in the next town.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's called trade. Most of us call it walking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nobody's selling. They're all waiting for a better price.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we wait too. Or starve politely.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Desert prices. Everything comes in on a mule's back.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the mule wants paying too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Buy what you can before the next carts don't come.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Grim way to go shopping.

who: two hawkers crying their wares

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Laces! Pins! Needles!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You've shouted that since dawn.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And I'll shout it till dusk. It's a living.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nobody buys laces when there's no bread.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Shout 'bread', then. See what happens.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Holy medals, blessed at the temple!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Blessed by whom?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: By me. I'm very devout.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ribbons from Sunward! Pins from Stonepass!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pins from the smithy round the corner.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hush.

who: townsfolk watching a caravan come in

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Caravan's in! Who's the master?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Thomas Gray, out of Sunward. Jewels and coin, they say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And dust. Always dust.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half the wagons. Where's the rest?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: On the road somewhere, with new owners.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Agnes atte Brook's carts. Cloth and fish again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Honest woman. Losing money every week, I hear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: John atte Green's back with the ingots.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not a scratch on him. The Reavers like him, somehow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Or he pays them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is there grain on those carts?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's iron. You can't eat iron.

who: two pedlars on their rounds

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Needles, salt, news from town!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How much for the news?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: News is free. The salt isn't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three hamlets today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And one pair of boots between us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then you walk barefoot tomorrow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They'll trade eggs for needles.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Take the eggs. Coin's thin in hungry country.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hamlet folk will want news of the raid.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tell it true?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tell it worse. Fear sells salt.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't take the north road.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Slavers?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Slavers. They'd sell us for less than our packs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fen folk pay in eels.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Eels don't fit in a purse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then they go in the pack.

who: two fishwives at the fish stall

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fresh fish!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sniff it first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't sniff it. Buy it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Catch was thin. Mostly bones.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sell the bones to the soup-wives.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fish heads, a penny each.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Heads only?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The tails went yesterday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pike this long, and the lady's cook wants three.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then charge the lady's price.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Reedwatch carp. Tastes of mud.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tastes of Reedwatch, then.

who: a woodcutter and his lad selling firewood

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dry oak, split and stacked.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Dry? It's hissing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's sighing. Different thing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The lord's foresters fined me for this load.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then put the fine on top of the price.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cold nights, thin purses. They burn their stools first.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then sell to the ones with stools left.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half the town's buying for winter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Raise it a penny. Nobody freezes over a penny.

who: two eel-sellers at their tubs

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eels! Live eels!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That one's dead.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's resting.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eels are the only thing the fens give freely.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the Crows take the rest.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nobody's turning eel down this week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They turned it down at harvest. Now they're grateful.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jellied or smoked?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Whatever's left. And what's left is smoked.

who: a poultry-wife and a buyer

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fat geese! Laying hens!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That hen hasn't laid since spring.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: She's thinking about it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Capons for the keep's feast.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The steward pays slow, but he pays.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fox got half the coop.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fox, or the lord's huntsmen?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Same thing, to a hen.

who: a leech-gatherer and an infirmary lay sister

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Leeches, freshly caught.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Freshly? They caught you, by the look of your legs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sister buys a dozen a week for the infirmary.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bad blood in the town, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Guild came back bloodied. Leeches will sell.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Leeches won't fix a Blight wound.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. But a Blight wound will buy them.

who: an outlaw and a fence haggling over plunder

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where'd you get this sword?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Found it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: On a man?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He didn't need it any more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rift gear. There's grey on the blade.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't buy it. The Blight sticks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Crows' knives, off the bodies.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fence them quiet. Their cousins buy them back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lord's seal on this cup.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Melt the seal. Sell the silver.

who: two Low-Water bandits holding the ford

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pennies for the ford, friend.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Since when is the ford yours?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Since we stood in it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two pennies a head, one a goat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the priest?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Priests pay triple. They've got God's purse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lord's hero is coming, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then raise the toll and spend it before he gets here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nobody's crossing. Too poor to pay.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then take their boots.

who: two toll-keepers at the town gate

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Toll's a penny. Carts two.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I've only a penny.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the cart stays.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Steward's doubled the gate toll.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: On a starving town? He'll get stones, not pennies.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Coin's pouring in at the gate.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And half of it pouring into {steward}'s purse.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Merchants won't pay toll for a road that loses carts.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tell them the toll pays for guards.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What guards?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Even the dust pays toll here.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Coin would toll the wind if it stopped long enough.

who: two sellswords newly in a lord's pay

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} has signed us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: For how long?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Till the coin runs out, or we do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Grey Company holds the ford now, on the lord's coin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And his own garrison sulks in the hall.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half up front. The rest after.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: After what?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: After we're alive to collect it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rich town, rich contract.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Rich towns pay late. Poor ones pay never.

who: two hired hands on wage day

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Count it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I counted. It's short.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's always short. Count it again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Paid in grain, not coin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Can't drink grain at the inn.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You can if you brew it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Silver! Real silver, with a face on it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Spend it fast. Faces change.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wage day. First round's mine.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the last three are mine, as ever.

who: an exile and the one who walks them to the gate

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Out by sundown, {lord} says.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Where will you go?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where nobody knows my face.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No town takes an exile.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The bands will.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's what frightens me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Juliana's gone to the refuge by First Hearth.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exiled, and the water costs what it cost.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The clan has struck your name.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then I've no name. Lighter to carry.

who: the warlock's apprentice and a water-carrier at the last spring

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Every load pays. The spring is warded.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And if they won't?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the water turns to sand in their skins.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The water-sellers are muttering.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let them. The spring answers to Juliana.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: John Robson keeps the wards up alone now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Does he know how?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He knows enough to frighten carriers.

who: two water-sellers paying Juliana's toll

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A copper a skin to the warlock.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And three from the buyer, to make it back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: She looked at me and my mule went still.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pay and don't look. That's the trick.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oasis folk can't pay what we charge now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then they thirst. Juliana won't lower her toll.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Company of the Lantern's coming, I hear.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: If they win, we're rich.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: If they lose, we're cinders.

who: two water-sellers at the market

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Clean water! Spring water!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: From the last spring?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: From a spring. Don't ask which.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Water's dearer than ale this week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then drink ale. The priests won't mind.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two pennies a cup.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: For water? Thieves.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thirsty thieves pay.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Folk say {calamity} sours the wells.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good for us. Bad for everyone else.

who: two Red Lances at a lord's gate

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Robert atte Lane, captain of the Red Lances. We seek a lord.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wait outside. {lord} is at the hunt.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eight good lances, cheap.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Cheap lances break.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ours break other men.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} can't feed his own garrison.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then he needs us more, not less.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sir Robert's steward kept us waiting all day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He keeps everyone waiting. It's how he counts them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bands are swelling again. Lords need swords.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then why does every lord say no?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Buy us a drink and hear our terms.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'm a cooper.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Coopers can hire swords too.

who: two Red Lances turned away from a keep

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Refused again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What did he say?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nothing. The steward said it for him.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Five keeps. Five doors shut.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we feed ourselves. The old way.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't say that aloud.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Coin laughed at our price.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He'll pay it to the Jackals and call it charity.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Lances are hungry, captain.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we squeeze the farmsteads. Gently. For now.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ironhand says clansmen don't hire southerners.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Clansmen don't pay wages either. Ask the Reavers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Greybeard has the Grey Company. Why would he want us?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because the Grey Company costs more.

who: two townsfolk talking of someone who got away

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He climbed the wall at night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: With those legs?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fear's good for the legs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A girl walked in from the north. Escaped the holds.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Alone? Then the slavers will want her back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The prisoner's gone from the cells.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Guard asleep again?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Guard paid, more like.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep running. Don't look at the lights.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Those are the hamlet's lights.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then run toward them.

who: two witnesses to a killing

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did you see? Right there in the street.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I saw nothing. You saw nothing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But...

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nothing, {A}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Knifed over a sack of {good}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Over the price, you mean.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That was {player}'s work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Shout it, then. Watch who comes for you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Killed for a loaf. A whole man, for one loaf.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hungry men count differently.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They've killed {dead}. By the ford, purse cut.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Crows, or the toll-takers?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does it matter to {dead} now?

who: two neighbours noticing someone has left

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where's the cooper?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Gone. Packed up in the night.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Owed me two pennies, too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three families gone this week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Gone where?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Anywhere with bread.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Some went out to the camp by the walls.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Some just walked. Can't blame them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Joined the Crows, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Half the fens have a cousin in the Crows.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hard to leave a thriving town.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Love managed it. She went off with a carter.

who: a townsperson summoned by Margaret the Sage and a friend

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Margaret the Sage sent for me.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: For you? What does a sage want with a dyer?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I don't know. That's the worst of it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Like the cobbler in the market. Remember?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I remember he couldn't stop weeping after.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The priest says don't go.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The priest isn't the one she summoned.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The leylines hum louder since she came.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hush. Not where people listen.

who: someone newly awakened and a worried friend

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My hands are warm all the time now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fever?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. Something woke.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: She touched him and his eyes caught fire.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Robert Cordwainer? He's at the tower school now.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The tower school will want you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And {lord} will want me sworn. I'd rather mend shoes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The lords fear what the sage wakes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lords fear anything they can't tax.

who: a hamlet headman and a carter handing over stores

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two sacks, a cheese, a cask.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sign for it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I can't write.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then make your mark and pray it's enough.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {steward} takes the hamlet's stores for the garrison.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And leaves us the sacks to chew.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Leave it at the woods' edge. The Crows collect.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's how a hamlet stays unburned.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Provisions for the escort, from {steward}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Short again.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The escort's short again too.
